title: [Bug]: GatedDeltaNet metadata builder classifies a stateless first chunk as a decode (same root cause as #51483)
body:
## Summary

The shared `GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder` classifies a request's first one-token chunk as a decode. Because the decode path reads its linear-attention state slot without zeroing it, and mamba-style state pages are not zeroed on reallocation, such a request would read whatever recurrent and conv state the previous owner of its recycled block left behind. #51483 fixes this for the `KimiK3KDAMetadataBuilder` subclass (Kimi-K3's full-rank-gate KDA path), but the base builder and every other model on it are unaffected by that change, so this is filed separately.

Models on the unmodified base builder, and so in scope: Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, OLMo-hybrid, InternS2-Mobius, Bailing-MoE-v3, and standalone Kimi-Linear (`KimiLinearForCausalLM`, whose `KimiGatedDeltaNetAttention` does not override the backend the way Kimi-K3 does). Their MTP and drafter variants reuse the same base builder.

This is a distinct defect from #49918 / PR #47123; see "Relationship to #49918" below.

## Mechanism

The full write-up for the Kimi case is in #51483; the shared-layer version:

- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py:213` calls `split_decodes_and_prefills(m, decode_threshold=1)` with the default `treat_short_extends_as_decodes=True`, so every row with `query_len <= 1` counts as a decode, including a row that has never been forwarded (`num_computed_tokens == 0`).
- `has_initial_state` is computed only when `num_prefills > 0` (`gdn_attn.py:391-392`). An all-one-token batch is all decodes, so `num_prefills == 0` and `has_initial_state` is `None`.
- The decode path then reads the recurrent state slot with no `has_initial_state` gate and no zero-fill. In the OLMo layer that is `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule(initial_state=ssm_state, ssm_state_indices=non_spec_state_indices_tensor, ...)` on the `num_decodes > 0` branch (`olmo_gdn_linear_attn.py`); in the Qwen layer it is `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` / `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode` with `initial_state=ssm_state` on the `num_decodes > 0` branches (`qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py`), and the conv update on the same branch (`causal_conv1d_update`) reads its slot the same way. The prefill path, by contrast, gates on `has_initial_state` and so zeroes a stateless slot.
- Mamba-style state pages are not zeroed on reallocation: the mamba spec is not in the worker-side zero-on-allocation set (`single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:86`).

Putting those together: a freshly admitted request whose block was previously owned by another request would read that request's leftover recurrent and conv state instead of a zero state. That is a correctness bug on its own, and it is also a path by which a corrupted (NaN) state block can be inherited by a new request. I have verified the misclassification and the unconditional decode read directly (see below); I have not run an end-to-end generation showing a recycled block still holding a prior request's state, so treat the inheritance step as a consequence of the code path rather than an observed failure.

The trigger is a scheduler step whose batch is entirely one-token rows and includes at least one first chunk. On default flags these models resolve to `mamba_cache_mode="align"` (like Kimi-K3), where a plain one-token prompt admitted alongside decodes is the reachable trigger; the budget-clamped first chunk (`scheduler.py:922`) is additionally gated by `_mamba_block_aligned_split` and reaches one token only when align is off or `long_prefill_token_threshold` / `max_num_batched_tokens` is below the mamba block size. A batch with any longer row is unaffected.

## What I verified

- Ran the real `GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build` on `seq_lens=[100, 50, 1]`, `query_lens=[1, 1, 1]`, `is_prefilling=[False, False, True]`: it returns 3 decodes, 0 prefills, `has_initial_state=None`, the same wrong classification the Kimi subclass gave before #51483.
- Confirmed by reading that the OLMo and Qwen GDN decode branches read `ssm_state` unconditionally on the `num_prefills == 0` route, while their prefill paths gate on `has_initial_state`.

## Relationship to #49918 / PR #47123

#49918 (and its fix PR #47123, which touches only `_is_uniform_decode` in `gpu_model_runner.py`) is a different root cause with a similar symptom: a `K+1`-token prompt under speculative decoding is misdispatched to the captured FULL spec-verify cudagraph by the runner's shape-only `_is_uniform_decode`, and the recurrent-state *write* is skipped. There the builder correctly reports `num_prefills > 0`. The defect here is the opposite at the builder level: the builder reports `num_prefills == 0` for a non-spec first chunk, and the decode path performs a stale *read*. #47123 does not touch `split_decodes_and_prefills` or the non-spec classification, so it does not fix this.

## Suggested fix

The same shape as #51483: classify by state rather than query length in the base builder (a first chunk with no computed tokens is a prefill; a resumed one-token chunk stays a decode), masked with the runner's `is_prefilling` flag so the cudagraph capture dummy batch is not promoted, and re-key the base cudagraph staging guard to the condition the dispatcher uses. The staging guard differs from Kimi's, so it needs its own measurement across the affected models. I am happy to open that PR once #51483 settles, or to defer to a maintainer who owns this backend.

## Environment

vLLM current main; observed on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell and RTX 5050 (sm_120), torch 2.13.0+cu130.

## Tool assistance

Claude Code was used for the investigation and for drafting this report. I reviewed every claim, ran the builder as described, and read the cited paths.

title: [Bugfix][GDN] Fix stateless first-chunk classification
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #51562.

`GDNMetadataBuilder.build()` passed `decode_threshold=1` to
`split_decodes_and_prefills()` while leaving
`treat_short_extends_as_decodes=True`. As a result, every one-token sequence was
classified as a decode, including the first chunk of a request with no prior GDN
state. The decode path then reads recurrent and convolution state unconditionally;
because Mamba-style state pages can be reused without being zeroed, that first token
could consume stale state from a previous request.

This change:

- classifies non-speculative one-token chunks from state availability
  (`seq_len <= query_len`) and the runner's `is_prefilling` signal;
- keeps resumed one-token chunks and CUDA graph capture dummy batches on the decode
  path;
- stages FULL CUDA graph metadata based on graph-compatible shape rather than the
  derived prefill/decode split, so mixed and all-stateless batches use persistent
  buffers correctly; and
- adds regression coverage for stateless first chunks, resumed one-token chunks,
  capture dummy metadata, and CUDA graph staging.

The fix lives in the shared GDN metadata builder and therefore covers its Qwen,
OLMo, InternS2, Bailing, and standalone Kimi-Linear users. Runner-level FULL CUDA
graph selection is a separate concern tracked by #47123; this PR does not duplicate
that broader runner change.

Duplicate-work check (2026-08-09): issue #51562 has no comments, and searches for
open PRs referencing `51562` or matching `GatedDeltaNet metadata stateless decode`
returned no results. Related PR #51483 changes the Kimi K3 subclass rather than this
shared builder.

AI assistance was used to inspect the issue, identify the root cause.  I reviewed the final diff and the test results below.The submitting author reviewed every changed line in the final diff.

## Test Plan

1. Run the GDN metadata builder unit tests.
2. Run Ruff lint and formatting checks on both changed files.
3. Before marking the PR ready, run an end-to-end affected-model evaluation with a
   freshly allocated/reused GDN state page and a one-token first chunk.

## Test Result

- Before the fix, the new stateless-first-chunk regression observed 3 decodes and 0
  prefills instead of 2 decodes and 1 prefill.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py`: **16 passed**, 14 existing
  PyTorch JIT deprecation warnings.

title: [Bug]: Prefill misdispatched into spec-decode FULL cudagraph when prompt length == 1 + num_speculative_tokens → silent GDN state loss, garbage output (hybrid/Qwen3-Next models)
body:
## Summary

When speculative decoding is enabled, a **prefill** whose scheduled token count happens to equal `uniform_decode_query_len * num_reqs` is misclassified as a uniform-decode batch and dispatched into the **FULL cudagraph captured for spec-decode**. For hybrid models with GDN/linear-attention layers (e.g. Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5-MoE), this silently skips **all recurrent-state writes** for that request: every subsequent decode step then computes from a zero initial state, producing deterministic garbage output and a collapsed draft acceptance rate.

The trigger is absurdly easy to hit: with `num_speculative_tokens=2`, **any 3-token prompt** (e.g. the Chinese prompt `中国的首都是` under the Qwen tokenizer) poisons the request from its very first step.

I have root-caused this with per-block checksums of the GDN state pools and verified a one-line-of-logic fix. Code on current `main` is identical to what I debugged on 0.27.1.

## Root cause

`GPUModelRunner._is_uniform_decode` (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py) is a **pure shape check**:

```python
return (
    ((max_num_scheduled_tokens == uniform_decode_query_len)
     and (num_tokens == max_num_scheduled_tokens * num_reqs))
    if force_uniform_decode is None
    else force_uniform_decode
)
```

With MTP `k=2`, `uniform_decode_query_len = 1 + 2 = 3`. A virgin single request whose prompt is exactly 3 tokens gives `max_num_scheduled_tokens == 3` and `num_tokens == 3 * 1`, so the **prefill** is classified as uniform decode and `cudagraph_dispatcher.dispatch(..., uniform_decode=True)` routes it into the FULL graph captured for spec-decode.

The failure mechanism for GDN layers:

1. The GDN metadata builder correctly classifies the step as a prefill (`num_prefills=1, num_spec_decodes=0`), **but** the persistent-buffer refresh in `GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build()` only happens in the spec/decode branches (gated on `num_prefills == 0`). A prefill build never touches the persistent buffers.
2. The FULL graph replays with **stale capture-time metadata**: `spec_state_indices_tensor` still holds `0 == NULL_BLOCK_ID` from `build_for_cudagraph_capture`.
3. The FLA kernels (`fused_recurrent`, `fused_sigmoid_gating`) and `causal_conv1d_update` all have null-block guards that **silently skip stores** when the state index is `NULL_BLOCK_ID` — correct padding hygiene, but here it swallows the entire prefill state write.
4. The request's conv/SSM states stay zero forever. The first sampled token already diverges; everything after is computed from a wrong recurrent state → deterministic garbage, and the drafter (whose own state is equally poisoned) gets ~0% acceptance.

## Measured evidence

Same weights, same 3-token greedy prompt, per-block checksums of the GDN state pools after the prefill step (instrumented `execute_model` with `torch.cuda.synchronize`):

| Config | state blocks written by the prefill | output |
|---|---|---|
| `PIECEWISE` (healthy) | `{1, 4, 7}` (target model, matching the request's block-table rows) + `{10}` (draft) | correct, deterministic |
| `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` (bug) | **only `{10}`** (draft runs piecewise); target blocks stay all-zero | deterministic garbage from token 1 |

Weight checksum identical in both boots; capture leaves the pools clean (all-zero before the first real step in both). Acceptance rate on mixed probes: 12% (bug) vs 79% (fixed/piecewise/eager).

This also explains the confusing symptom pattern that made the bug look like a "speculative rejection/rollback corruption" (#40880-style reports): prompts that don't tokenize to exactly `1+k` tokens are dispatched normally and stay healthy, genuine uniform-decode FULL replays are correct (the spec branch does refresh persistent buffers), and the garbage is byte-identical across reboots because everything is deterministic.

## Reproduction

vLLM 0.27.1 (logic identical on current main), Qwen3.5-MoE hybrid (30 GDN + 10 full-attn layers), 1 GPU:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-MoE-FP8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}'

curl http://localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "...", "prompt": "中国的首都是", "max_tokens": 24, "temperature": 0}'
# prompt must tokenize to exactly (1 + num_speculative_tokens) tokens; garbage output.
# Same request with cudagraph_mode PIECEWISE or --enforce-eager → correct output.
```

Note the aliasing is generic: any batch of fresh `num_reqs` prompts scheduled as exactly `(1+k)` tokens each hits the same path, and `q_len==1` aliasing with 1-token prompts at `k=0` is possible in principle too.

## Suggested fix (verified locally)

Uniform-decode classification should require every request in the batch to actually be **past its prompt**, not just match the shape:

```python
def _is_uniform_decode(self, *, max_num_scheduled_tokens, uniform_decode_query_len,
                       num_tokens, num_reqs, force_uniform_decode=None):
    if force_uniform_decode is not None:   # keep capture-path bypass
        return force_uniform_decode
    if not (max_num_scheduled_tokens == uniform_decode_query_len
            and num_tokens == max_num_scheduled_tokens * num_reqs):
        return False
    ib = self.input_batch
    return bool((ib.num_computed_tokens_cpu[:num_reqs]
                 >= ib.num_prompt_tokens[:num_reqs]).all())
```

Aliased prefill batches then fall back to the PIECEWISE path (which is where prefills belong anyway); genuine uniform decodes keep the FULL graph. Verified on my deployment: garbage gone (byte-exact vs piecewise golden on the trap prompt), acceptance restored 12%→79%, no measurable perf regression (FULL graph retained for real decode batches; a 100k-context needle gate and short-decode throughput both match or beat the eager baseline).


## Related issues

- #28015 — the inverse aliasing (uniform-decode batches mis-shaped by padding for MLA backends); same root class: shape-only dispatch classification.
- #40880 / #40914 — Qwen3-Next hybrid × MTP × cudagraph degraded output; the fix merged there was TurboQuant-specific and this mechanism explains the remaining reports.
- #34571, #39273, vllm-ascend#7148 — adjacent mamba/GDN spec-decode state-corruption reports.

## Environment

vLLM 0.27.1 (bug verified byte-identical in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` on current main), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 (Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration, 30 GDN + 10 full-attn), MTP k=2, fp8 KV, single ROCm gfx1151 GPU — the bug is in platform-independent dispatch logic (also reproduced with two different attention backends).

title: [Bugfix] Reject shape-aliased prefills in uniform-decode classification
body:
## Purpose

FIX #53051 (same root cause as #49918)

With spec decode enabled, `GPUModelRunner._is_uniform_decode` classifies batches by shape only. A prefill whose scheduled tokens equal `uniform_decode_query_len (= 1 + num_spec_tokens)` per request — e.g. a single (k+1)-token prompt — aliases the uniform-decode shape and is dispatched into the FULL cudagraph captured for spec decode. For attention backends with persistent metadata buffers (e.g. GDN / hybrid recurrent models), those buffers are only refreshed on the decode path, so the replay uses stale capture-time state indices (NULL block 0); the kernels' null-block guards silently skip all recurrent-state writes, the request's state stays zero forever, and output is deterministic garbage (details and measured evidence in #53051).

This PR makes `_is_uniform_decode` additionally require that every request in the batch is already past its prompt (`num_computed_tokens >= num_prompt_tokens`), so any batch still containing prefill tokens falls back to the mixed prefill-decode path. The `force_uniform_decode` override used for cudagraph capture is preserved unchanged.

**Relationship to #47123:** that PR addresses the same root cause by computing `force_uniform_decode=False` in `execute_model` when a hybrid model's batch contains context requests. This PR is an alternative that fixes the classification at its source instead: the diff is smaller (no new caller-side state), it applies to all models rather than only `is_hybrid` (the q_len==1 aliasing of 1-token prompts exists without spec decode too), and the per-request check also covers chunked-prefill last chunks and mixed batches uniformly. If maintainers prefer the approach in #47123, I'm happy to close this one in its favor.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py -k uniform_decode`
  - existing `test_is_uniform_decode` cases preserved (adapted to the method now reading `self.input_batch`)
  - new `test_is_uniform_decode_rejects_shape_aliased_prefill`: aliased (k+1)-token prompt, chunked-prefill last chunk, mixed decode+prefill batch, 1-token prompt without spec decode, and the `force_uniform_decode` capture override
- The new regression test fails against the pre-fix shape-only logic and passes with the fix.

## Test Result

Unit tests pass. End-to-end, the same per-request check (as a hot patch on v0.27.1, ROCm gfx1151, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B GDN hybrid, MTP k=2, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`) was validated in the deployment from #53051:

- the aliased 3-token prompt's output recovers to byte-identical with the eager reference (previously deterministic garbage)
- GDN state-write signature during the aliased prefill restored from draft-only `{10}` to full `{1, 4, 7, 10}`
- spec-decode acceptance rate on subsequent traffic recovers 12% → 79%
- no regression in decode throughput or 100k-token long-context gates

title: [Bugfix][GDN] Reclassify a partial final speculative group as prefill at the max-model-len boundary
body:
## Problem

A completion that ends at exactly `max-model-len` yields one **incomplete** speculative token group (fewer than `num_speculative_tokens + 1` tokens). `GDNAttentionMetadataBuilder.build()` still classifies the batch as pure spec decode and hands the fused GDN kernels a batch that violates their complete-group invariant (`spec_token == num_spec_decodes * (num_speculative_tokens + 1)`), so the final tokens of an exact full-context generation can never complete.

Repro: MTP4 on a GDN-hybrid Qwen checkpoint — a 131,072-token completion stalled at 124/128 outputs because the last step produced a 4-token group instead of 5.

## Fix

In the pure-spec branch, detect the truncated final group and reclassify it as a **stateful non-spec prefill** (the prefill path already handles initial state). Complete groups are untouched. The classification lives in the shared builder, so every backend benefits; the kernel-side complete-group TORCH_CHECK stays intact as a live guard.

Sizing invariants of the reclassified batch, `N` = reclassified spec rows — sized by `N` alone, never the padded batch size (which may carry trailing zero-length sequences): `num_spec_decodes=0`, spec fields `None`, `num_prefills=N`, `non_spec_query_start_loc(_cpu) = query_start_loc(_cpu)[:N + 1]`, `non_spec_state_indices = block_table[:N, 0]`, `has_initial_state = (computed_tokens > 0)[:N]`, `num_accepted_tokens=None`.

## Tests (3 new)

- `test_gdn_build_classification[partial_final_spec_group_at_max_len_uses_full_group]` — truncated step classifies as `num_prefills=2`, `num_spec_decodes=0`.
- `test_partial_final_spec_group_reclassified_as_prefill` — no spec metadata leaks; `non_spec_query_start_loc.tolist() == [0, 3, 5]`.
- `test_partial_final_spec_group_padded_batch_shapes` — with a trailing zero-length padded sequence, asserts the fused-op sizing above (values `[0, 3, 5]`, `[True, True]`) — the padded row is sliced out, not leaked.

## Verification

CPU-only (no GPU) in `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu@sha256:f01e24f6c7ff01f1e0662234255a1372297d1dbd89d003cf13c8fad3eab1ba4f` (`vllm 0.27.2rc1.dev77+gac7509e2b`, torch `2.13.0+xpu`): `pytest -p no:cacheprovider -v tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py`.

Regression-first — padded test against a build without the `[:N]` slices (padded row leaks `[0, 3, 5, 5]`):

```
E       AssertionError: assert 4 == ((2 + 0) + 1)
================== 1 failed, 11 passed, 22 warnings in 47.33s ==================
```

With the slices: `12 passed, 22 warnings in 43.27s`, exit 0.

Kernel-contract checks (`TORCH_CHECK(spec_token == num_spec_decodes * (num_speculative_tokens + 1))` etc.) verified against `vllm-xpu-kernels` `gdn_attn_interface.cpp`; on-device evidence follows in a comment.

## Not #391 (vllm-xpu-kernels)

#391 (open, 2026-06-03, @ehartford/QuixiAI, fixes #389) relaxes metadata *shape* checks for graph-padded buffers whose groups are still complete, leaving the uniform-stride invariant intact. This PR handles a *genuinely ragged* final group by reclassifying it out of the spec path upstream of the kernel.

## Related, none claiming this fix (checked 2026-09-05)

#50623 (cudagraph padding branch, different condition) · #50021 (accepted-token bounds, kernel-side) · #37052 (`block_table` OOB, different bug) · #55404 (merged; rewrote `build_for_cudagraph_capture` above this region — diff regenerated after it, applies at exact hunk positions).
